Important Parliamentary Devices:
• Question Hour
• Zero Hour
• Motions
• No-Confidence Motion
• Adjournment Motion
Important Parliamentary Devices:• Question Hour• Zero Hour• Motions• No-Confidence Motion• Adjournment Motion

rows: First hour of a sitting dedicated to asking and answering questions (Starred, Unstarred, Short Notice).
Informal Indian innovation starting immediately after Question Hour for urgent matters without prior notice.
Extraordinary procedure to discuss an urgent matter of public importance; requires 50 members' support.
Moved in Lok Sabha to test if the Council of Ministers holds majority confidence.

items: Zero Hour is an informal device unique to Indian parliamentary practice and is NOT mentioned in the Rules of Procedure.
A No-Confidence Motion requires the support of at least 50 members and can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
An Adjournment Motion carries an element of censure against the government.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Question Hour and Zero Hour form the core time-based procedural devices in Parliament.
Motions enable members to bring specific subjects forward for discussion and voting.
The No-Confidence Motion is a critical tool to assess whether the ruling government retains the confidence of the House.
The Adjournment Motion allows the House to set aside normal business to address a matter of urgent public importance.
